items.summary: Tesla reduced its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to roughly US$20 billion, down from US$25 billion, while reporting US$1.53 billion in free cash flow for the third quarter ended Sept 30. CEO Elon Musk has discussed a potential merger with SpaceX, which he described as a 'good idea,' though he stated on Oct 21 that he had no further comments. Analysts note that while the cash flow is positive, the lower spending on AI and robotics raises questions about the company's growth strategy as it prepares for a potential deal with the capital-intensive space venture.
items.title: Tesla Cuts Spending Ahead of Potential SpaceX Merger While Musk Bets on AI

items.summary: NVIDIA announced collaborations with global healthcare and research organizations to advance protein design, drug discovery, and cancer care. NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design debuted RFD4-Proteina, an open model combining programmable protein design with search capabilities. Siemens Healthineers is collaborating with NVIDIA to develop adaptive radiotherapy using agentic co-planning and simulation. Various companies, including Benchling, Biolevate, and Automata, are using NVIDIA BioNeMo to develop scientific agents. NVIDIA open models and accelerated computing aim to help experts evaluate possibilities faster, from designing proteins to planning treatment. David Baker, a 2024 Nobel Laureate, noted the shift toward designing new proteins. Arthur Kaindl emphasized that adaptive radiotherapy should adapt to the patient. By 2050, approximately 35 million people worldwide are projected to be diagnosed with cancer each year. Global scientific R&D reaches $3. 8 trillion, and annual pharmaceutical budgets approach $300 billion.
items.title: NVIDIA Partners with Healthcare Leaders to Advance Drug Discovery and Cancer Care

items.summary: Apple has introduced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone, with a starting price of S$3,099. The device features a 7.6-inch OLED internal display and a 5.4-inch outer screen, powered by the A20 Pro chip. Unlike previous models, it lacks Face ID, utilizing Touch ID instead. The phone offers IP68 water resistance and includes a 48MP dual-camera system with 4x optical zoom. While the crease is nearly invisible, the device is designed for right-handed use only. Apple suggests a 512GB storage model for optimal performance and recommends an iCloud+ subscription for full functionality.
items.title: Apple Unveils Foldable iPhone Duo with Premium Features and High Price

items.summary: Reliance Industries leaders Mukesh and Anant Ambani hosted US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US Ambassador Sergio Gor at the Jamnagar refinery. The visit included tours of the facility and New Energy projects, alongside discussions on energy security and commercial partnerships. Rubio's trip also involved talks with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar regarding the India-US strategic partnership and trade negotiations.
items.title: Reliance Leaders Host US Officials at Jamnagar Refinery

items.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $US25 billion after a jury found the company liable for deceiving users about Facebook privacy. This marks the largest fine ever against the tech giant. The ruling stems from a jury finding Meta responsible for over 43 million violations of state consumer protection laws regarding misleading statements about data handling. While Meta plans to appeal, citing the penalty as a tax on speech, New Mexico Attorney-General Raúl Torrez stated the judgment signals accountability for Silicon Valley. The funds will support state education, though the final amount may change during the appeal process.
items.title: New Mexico Orders Meta $25 Billion Privacy Fine

items.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg agreed to stay in California for eight years, linking his ability to sell shares to his residence. This decision follows a board dinner where he considered leaving due to Proposition 40, a potential 5% billionaire tax. While recent polling suggests the measure may fail, the agreement includes a special share class to help cover any taxes owed if it passes.
items.title: Meta CEO Agrees to Remain in California Amid Tax Measure

items.summary: Tesla announced plans to sell the Cybercab to consumers by the end of 2026, featuring a design with no steering wheel or pedals. During a Q3 conference call, VP of Engineering Lars Moravy confirmed this timeline, while Ashok Ellus clarified that unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) software will not be available to customers until Q2 2027. The article notes a potential six-month gap where the vehicles would lack necessary software for operation. Tesla also stated that Robotaxis would cover half the US population by the end of last year, though they are currently limited to six cities in two states. The report questions the practicality of selling a vehicle that cannot be driven or parked without a steering wheel.
items.title: Tesla Announces Cybercab Launch and Autonomous Driving Timeline

items.summary: Google Chrome is introducing new scam protections powered by Gemini to detect deceptive websites and warn users against ClickFix attacks. These updates are part of Enhanced Protection in Safe Browsing, which Google claims makes users ten times safer from phishing and social engineering compared to Standard Protection. The browser will also display new 'suspicious site' warnings for pages showing deceptive patterns that do not yet meet the threshold for full-page red warnings. Additionally, Chrome will now analyze clipboard payloads for malicious commands and remove personally identifiable information before sending them to Safe Browsing for analysis.
items.title: Google Chrome Adds Gemini-Powered Scam Detection and ClickFix Warnings

items.summary: Google Cloud released llm-d 1.0, the first stable version of its distributed inference stack, at the PyTorch Conference North America. The open-source project, founded in 2025 by Red Hat, IBM, Google Cloud, CoreWeave, and NVIDIA, targets self-hosted agent and RL workloads. Google reports benchmark results from a 17,000-node GKE deployment showing a 2.4x throughput increase and an 85% reduction in median time-to-first-token on Ironwood TPUs. Other adopters, including Snap and Zenteiq, report similar performance gains. The release introduces features like cache-aware routing and multi-tenant quality of service.
items.title: Google Cloud Releases Stable llm-d 1.0 for Distributed Inference

items.summary: IBM finance chief James Kavanaugh stated that delayed software deals are closing, prompting a raised annual software revenue forecast of about 7 per cent to 8 per cent. The company reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings, with shares rising about 4 per cent in extended trading.
items.title: IBM Raises Software Revenue Outlook as Deal Delays Ease

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India rejected all bids in a treasury bill auction, causing yields to rise. The government aimed to raise ₹23,000 crores but faced higher yield bids. Market analysts suggest a potential 50 basis point rate hike in December due to high oil prices and global yield pressure. Anshul Chandak of RBL Bank noted that market conditions are unfavorable.
items.title: RBI Rejects T-Bill Bids Amid Rising Yields and Oil Prices

items.summary: Jefferies analysts caution that the IT sector's growth outlook remains muted through FY26-29, potentially driven by worsening sentiment on global AI capital expenditure. Despite this, the brokerage identifies valuation upside in select stocks, noting a lack of negative growth surprises. Consequently, Jefferies raised target prices for Infosys and TCS by 14-18% while maintaining hold and underperform ratings respectively.
items.title: Jefferies Sees Valuation Upside in Select IT Stocks Despite Muted Growth

items.summary: Texas Instruments forecast fourth-quarter revenue between $5.80 billion and $6.30 billion, exceeding analyst estimates of $5.73 billion. The company expects quarterly profit between $2.45 and $2.79 per share. CEO Haviv Ilan noted strong cash flow from operations of $9.9 billion over the trailing 12 months, highlighting the strength of its business model and product portfolio.
items.title: Texas Instruments Reports Strong Quarterly Revenue and Profit Growth

items.summary: The Supreme Court sought an explanation from the government regarding why a new crash relief scheme, offering Rs 2 lakh for deaths and Rs 1 lakh for grievous injuries, excludes uninsured vehicles. Officials stated the scheme is framed under the Central Motor Vehicle Act, which currently covers only insured vehicles, while cases involving uninsured vehicles are directed to the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal.
items.title: Supreme Court Questions Exclusion of Uninsured Vehicles from Crash Relief Scheme

items.summary: Rosatom Automated Control Systems has completed supplying engineered safety features actuation system computerised subsystems for units 3 and 4 of the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in Tamil Nadu. The delivery includes approximately 300 items, marking a step in equipping the facility with Russian automation and safety systems as part of an industrial cooperation project.
items.title: Rosatom Delivers Safety Systems for Kudankulam Units 3 and 4

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Jamnagar, Gujarat, to visit Reliance Industries Ltd's refinery and Vantara. His visit follows talks with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai regarding the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement.
items.title: Marco Rubio arrives in Jamnagar to visit Reliance refinery as India-US trade deal moves closer to final agreement

items.summary: Cygames canceled its first North American Umamusume concerts in Los Angeles on Oct. 20, just days before the scheduled Oct. 22 and 23 dates. The event, featuring 17 voice actors, was intended to showcase the multimedia franchise. The cancellation underscores the difficulties Japanese entertainers face when attempting to perform internationally despite growing demand.
items.title: Umamusume Concert Cancellation Highlights Visa Hurdles for Japanese Performers

items.summary: Irish lawmakers voted to scrap a UN approval requirement for overseas peacekeeping missions, approving the legislation by 79 votes to 71. The move, supported by Taoiseach Micheal Martin, aims to allow faster crisis response. Opposition parties, including Sinn Fein, warn it threatens Ireland's military neutrality and could lead to closer alignment with NATO structures.
items.title: Ireland Votes to Remove UN Veto on Peacekeeping Deployments

items.summary: A class action lawsuit filed in the Federal Court of Australia alleges that Meta Platforms' Facebook and Instagram exposed children to harmful content and utilized addictive algorithms. The suit, brought by MinterEllison on behalf of eight plaintiffs, claims the platforms harmed users under 18. Meta did not immediately respond to comment requests.
items.title: Meta Faces Australian Class Action Over Alleged Harm to Children

items.summary: Standard Chartered analysts project mixed outcomes for base metals in 2026 and 2027. Copper prices are expected to remain elevated due to supply stresses and U.S. tariff uncertainty, with forecasts raised to $13,674/t in 2026. Conversely, aluminum forecasts were lowered to $3,249/t in 2026 as Middle East supply risks eased and production in China and Indonesia recovered. Zinc forecasts were raised to $3,555/t, supported by tight concentrate markets, while nickel prices are projected to decline slightly. The outlook hinges on macroeconomic conditions, geopolitical developments, and specific supply chain disruptions.
items.title: Standard Chartered Forecasts Mixed Base Metal Prices Amid Supply and Tariff Uncertainty

items.summary: Leading global telecom operators are converting their networks into distributed intelligence platforms by integrating NVIDIA accelerated computing into centralized data centers, metro sites, and cell sites. T-Mobile completed the world's first AI-RAN call, while BT, Deutsche Telekom, Elisa, and Orange are running pilots or trials using Nokia's software on NVIDIA hardware. These operators aim to serve models and applications closer to users, improving wireless experiences and automating operations. Jensen Huang stated that telecom networks will now carry the world's intelligence, extending accelerated computing into the radio network itself to support AI-native 5G.
items.title: Telecom Operators Transform Networks Into Distributed AI Platforms

items.summary: Tesla has pushed the arrival of unsupervised Full Self-Driving to Q2 2027, but clarified it applies only to customer vehicles joining the company's managed Robotaxi fleet within specific zones. AI chief Ashok Elluswamy stated this represents a shift from the original promise of personal autonomous use. Current Robotaxi operations cover small areas in six US metros and remain limited by safety regulations, particularly in California where human drivers are still required. Analysts note the timeline is uncertain and the product scope is significantly narrower than previously marketed.
items.title: Tesla Delays Unsupervised FSD to 2027 for Robotaxi Fleet Only

items.summary: Experts describe Elon Musk's new flying Roadster as a publicity stunt rather than a viable vehicle. While Musk claims the car can fly and perform acrobatics, experts from QUT and the University of Melbourne question its safety and regulatory feasibility in Australia. They note the technology lacks a clear pathway to real-world use and warn of significant infrastructure challenges.
items.title: Experts Call Elon Musk's Flying Roadster a Publicity Stunt

items.summary: The U.S. National Security Agency issued a warning regarding two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a language powering roughly 70% of websites. OpenAI and Google's Wiz identified these flaws using AI models, noting that artificial intelligence has lowered the barrier for exploitation. The NSA advises immediate patching or taking sites offline until updates are applied.
items.title: NSA Warns of Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Discovered by AI Tools

items.summary: The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival, running from October 26 to November 4, showcases Japanese cinema ranging from golden age classics to independent films. Key titles include Takahisa Zeze’s “Sukiyaki,” opening the event, and Takashi Yamazaki’s “Godzilla Minus Zero,” serving as the November centerpiece. The festival continues its tradition of featuring diverse Japanese cinematic works.
items.title: Japanese Films Highlight Melodrama and Monsters at TIFF

items.summary: Indian midcap and smallcap indices have entered a correction phase, with the Nifty Midcap 150 falling 10.2% from its 52-week high. While valuations remain elevated compared to large-caps, analysts project 16-20% earnings growth for these segments. Experts note that while corrections are visible in individual stocks, the aggregate outlook remains supported by positive earnings projections.
items.title: Indian Midcap and Smallcap Indices Enter Correction Phase Amid Valuation Concerns

items.summary: A Saudi resident was killed and eight others injured when an attack struck King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, according to the Civil Aviation Authority. The airport sustained material damage, and aircraft were diverted. Saudi authorities and Houthi rebels have not identified the attackers. The incident follows wider strikes and a US order for diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia due to escalating conflict concerns.
items.title: Saudi Airport Attack Kills One, Injures Eight Amid Diplomatic Evacuation

items.summary: The US State Department ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia due to a barrage of near-daily attacks by the Iranian-supported Houthis. State department spokesperson Tommy Pigott stated that safety remains the highest priority. The order covers the embassy in Riyadh and satellite consulates, though reports of similar withdrawals in other Gulf nations were described as inaccurate by Pigott.
items.title: US State Department Orders Diplomats to Leave Saudi Arabia Amid Houthi Attacks

items.summary: AIPAC announced it will stop issuing endorsements and making direct PAC contributions to candidates, citing growing challenges. The group plans to shift toward mobilizing individual donors and increasing organized contributions. AIPAC contributed nearly $25 million in 2026 through September. Its affiliated super PAC spent $13 million on contributions and $53.5 million on independent expenditures. The organization faces criticism over its stances on issues like the wars in Gaza and Iran.
items.title: AIPAC Halts Direct Endorsements Amid Political Challenges

items.summary: Comcast Corp. is planning significant job cuts as part of a restructuring of its cable-TV, broadband, and wireless businesses. According to people familiar with the company's thinking, the reorganization aims to position Comcast as an independent entity following the spin-off of NBCUniversal next year. The cuts are intended to create a more nimble workforce and free up cash for growth opportunities.
items.title: Comcast Plans Significant Job Cuts Ahead of NBCUniversal Spin-Off

items.summary: The Indian rupee reached a six-week high, trading between 94.42 and 94.82, driven by inflows from the Jio Platforms IPO and a softer dollar index. While oil prices rose 1.3% to over $110 per barrel, causing some caution, RBI intervention helped the currency close stronger than 94.50 levels. Analysts note immediate support at the 94.30 level.
items.title: Rupee Rises on Jio IPO Inflows and Weaker Dollar

items.summary: SBI confirmed a data breach involving 3,897 customer records found on the dark web. The bank identified these records during a preliminary analysis of 3.75 lakh records. SBI activated incident response protocols and commissioned an independent agency to investigate the claim made by CyberPulse regarding a threat actor named Siriusim. The bank stated the incident had no material impact on its operations.
items.title: SBI Confirms Data Breach Involving Thousands of Customer Records

items.summary: Traffic congestion in Bhopal is attributed to poor road conditions and the unregulated movement of e-rickshaws and autorickshaws. These vehicles frequently park at busy crossings and intersections, causing bottlenecks. Although police intervene to clear these spots, the problem recurs quickly. Additional deputy commissioner Basant Kumar Kaul stated that intensified action against operators will follow the festive season.
items.title: Unregulated E-Rickshaws and Autos Worsen Traffic in Bhopal

items.summary: Police personnel and officers in Indore paid tribute to martyrs during a Commemoration Day ceremony at the 15th Battalion of the Special Armed Force. Commissioner Santosh Kumar Singh attended as chief guest. Officials noted that 154 police officers died nationwide between September 1, 2025, and August 31, 2026, with nine from Madhya Pradesh. The event commemorated the 1959 Ladakh attack and reaffirmed commitment to public safety.
items.title: Police in Indore Honor Martyrs on Commemoration Day

items.summary: A BBC InDepth article examines the prevalence of older US politicians, highlighting Hal Rogers as the longest-serving House member at 88. The piece notes that many senior figures, including Donald Trump and Chuck Grassley, remain in office while younger candidates like Riley Owen struggle against established incumbents with superior fundraising. Experts cite a 'gerontocracy' where the median age of Congress has risen significantly since the 1980s. Factors contributing to this trend include low youth voter turnout, high minimum age requirements for office, and a lack of paid parental leave. While some argue age correlates with experience, others emphasize that competency varies regardless of age, urging a focus on ideas rather than birth year.
items.title: US Politicians Face Aging Crisis and Youth Disengagement

items.summary: The US Department of Agriculture confirmed the first detection of the flesh-eating New World screwworm parasite in US wildlife, found in an elk in Pecos County, Texas. Officials are modifying infested zones and conducting surveillance. The pest, eradicated decades ago, has recently surged north from Central America, prompting import restrictions and affecting beef supplies.
items.title: USDA Confirms First Detection of Flesh-Eating Screwworm in US Wildlife

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey announced the UK's new Energy Wealth Fund, funded by £2bn diverted from the National Wealth Fund. Officials calculated that investing historical North Sea receipts could have created a trillion-pound sovereign wealth fund. While the new fund aims for domestic green energy investment, it may struggle to match Norway's performance, which grew significantly through foreign investments.
items.title: UK creates Energy Wealth Fund from diverted National Wealth money

items.summary: UAE Minister of State Lana Nusseibeh announced her candidacy for UN secretary-general following formal nomination by the United Arab Emirates. She stated she is running because 'this is a moment to act with greater urgency.' The nomination follows six failed Security Council voting rounds and the upcoming end of Antonio Guterres' term on Dec. 31, 2026.
items.title: UAE Minister Lana Nusseibeh Announces Candidacy for UN Secretary-General

items.summary: A survey indicates that over one in ten UK university students now plan to move abroad after graduation, an increase from 7.8% two years ago. This trend coincides with record-high competition for graduate jobs in the UK, where employers receive an average of 140 applications per vacancy. Destinations like Australia, the US, and the EU attract young Britons seeking better opportunities or quality of life. While some face lower salaries, others find improved funding or living conditions. Experts attribute this shift to high housing costs, student debt, and weak wage growth in the UK.
items.title: UK Graduates Seek Fresh Starts Abroad Amid Job Market Struggles

items.summary: The Trump administration is challenging federal permits for several offshore wind projects along the East Coast, including New England Wind and Revolution Wind. The Justice Department asked a court to review permits, arguing they do not adequately comply with the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act. This move follows similar requests to reconsider approvals for other projects. Critics argue this strategy undermines energy infrastructure development and threatens bipartisan permitting negotiations. While the administration claims it is complying with legal schedules rather than changing policy, experts warn it creates uncertainty for large infrastructure projects.
items.title: Trump Administration Targets Approved Offshore Wind Projects

items.summary: The US government suspended eight major technology firms, including Microsoft and Infosys, from hiring skilled international workers through the PERM program. This move aligns with stricter immigration rules under the Trump administration, aiming to reduce reliance on foreign talent. While firms like Wipro and Tata Consultancy Services report minimal impact due to high local hiring, the policy creates uncertainty for Indian professionals seeking permanent residency. Experts note that while business operations may remain stable, the human cost includes delayed green card applications and increased hostility toward South Asian immigrants. Alternative pathways for residency exist but may face future restrictions.
items.title: US suspends PERM visas for eight Indian tech firms amid immigration crackdown

items.summary: Oil supermajors are expected to report record profits following the Middle East conflict, with the Energy sector seeing 128.2% annual growth. Despite these gains, companies like Shell, BP, TotalEnergies, and Exxon are unlikely to increase capital expenditure. Instead, they plan to use windfall profits to pay down debt and conduct share buybacks. While some exploration spending continues in regions like Africa and South America, the industry maintains financial discipline, prioritizing balance sheet health over a spending spree, even as global demand for oil and gas remains robust.
items.title: Big Oil Companies Keep Profits High While Restraining Spending

items.summary: Blackstone veteran Jas Khaira argues that concerns regarding AI infrastructure debt are overblown. Speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt, Khaira highlighted Blackstone's $1.3 trillion in assets under management and its aggressive financing of neoclouds, such as a $5 billion commitment to Crux AI and a $2.3 billion loan to CoreWeave. While acknowledging rising debt burdens and market jitters, Khaira attributed recent volatility to higher interest rates and credit spreads rather than fundamental instability. He noted that most data center debt is backed by creditworthy hyperscalers. Beyond financing, Blackstone launched a $1.5 billion joint venture with Anthropic to help companies adopt AI.
items.title: Blackstone Executive Dismisses AI Infrastructure Debt Fears

items.summary: US envoy Steve Witkoff hailed Vladimir Putin as a 'true humanitarian' Wednesday following the release of an American prisoner and agreement to trilateral talks. Experts note the move fosters goodwill while costing Moscow little. Negotiations could resume next month, though previous February discussions failed. Kyiv fears Washington seeks to end the war on Moscow's terms, while President Trump expressed frustration over Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries amid high fuel prices.
items.title: US Envoy Witkoff Calls Putin Humanitarian After Prisoner Release

items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is urging US President Donald Trump to resume strikes against Iran amid concerns over upcoming elections. While Netanyahu reportedly planned attacks on Iranian infrastructure earlier this month, Trump has delayed the plan until after the US midterm elections on Nov. 3. Iranian officials warn that the US has limited military options or faces a more painful outcome.
items.title: Netanyahu Presses Trump to Strike Iran Before US Elections

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin released American Stephen Hubbard from a Russian prison following a request from President Trump. Hubbard, a 74-year-old former school teacher from Michigan, had been detained in 2022 for fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine. White House Envoy Steve Witkoff met with Putin in Saint Petersburg to discuss the release and broader peace proposals. Witkoff praised Putin as a humanitarian, a comment noted as unusual. Hubbard, who appeared healthy, is returning home. The U.S. stated it gave nothing in return, though recent American gestures toward Russia include agreeing to buy Russian diesel fuel and waiving sanctions.
items.title: Putin Frees American Stephen Hubbard After Trump Request

items.summary: Virginia's major investor-owned utilities have released the first public data quantifying annual grid utilization. Dominion Energy reported a 41% annual rate for its system serving Data Center Alley, while Appalachian Power reported 14% annually in rural areas. The filings highlight significant capacity during peak hours and spark debate over how to measure grid constraints. Regulators and advocates discuss whether these metrics should influence infrastructure investment decisions, with some arguing for faster adoption given rapid demand growth. The data aims to help determine if new infrastructure is needed or if existing assets can be used more efficiently through technologies like battery storage.
items.title: Virginia Utilities Report First Grid Utilization Metrics Amid Data Center Growth

items.summary: King Charles quoted a hadith of the Prophet Muhammad in Arabic during a state banquet for Sultan Haitham bin Tariq of Oman at Windsor Castle on Tuesday, 22 October 2026. The Sultan, visiting for the first time in 44 years, was welcomed by King Charles and Queen Camilla. Charles praised the people of Oman, stating they would not revile or beat visitors, a clip of which went viral. The monarch also highlighted the long partnership between the UK and Oman.
items.title: King Charles Recites Hadith in Arabic to Honor Oman

items.summary: Yemeni government forces and allied fighters clashed with Houthi fighters on the outskirts of Taiz on Wednesday, 21 October. The internationally recognised government stated its forces repelled the attack and reported air strikes on Houthi positions. Fighting continues as Houthi forces encircle the city, disrupting supply routes and waste collection, leading residents to fear death from shelling or rubbish.
items.title: Fighting Erupts in Taiz as Tanks Clash with Houthi Forces

items.summary: Thousands of students, teachers, and public-sector workers marched through central Athens on Wednesday, demanding increased education funding, smaller classes, and affordable housing. Police estimated around 10,000 participants in Athens and its suburbs, though organizers claimed a higher turnout. The demonstration, part of a broader European movement, ended peacefully shortly before 2pm, reflecting pressure on the Greek government to address student financial difficulties and education funding.
items.title: Thousands March in Athens for Education Funding and Housing

items.summary: Thousands of students, teachers, and public-sector workers marched through central Athens on Wednesday, demanding increased education funding, smaller classes, and affordable housing. Police estimated around 10,000 participants in Athens and its suburbs, though organizers claimed a higher turnout. The demonstration, part of a broader European movement, also saw rallies in Thessaloniki, Patras, Larissa, and Crete, ending peacefully before 2pm.
items.title: Thousands March in Athens for Education Funding and Housing

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV's doctors announced that no further treatment is necessary following his lung surgery. Histological and molecular analyses confirmed a localized pulmonary adenocarcinoma that had not spread beyond the lung. Dr. Luigi Carbone and Prof. Stefano Margaritora reported these findings, noting the tumor was contained and the pontiff requires no additional oncological therapy.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Requires No Further Treatment After Lung Surgery

items.summary: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced an additional fund of Rs 71,01,54,000 for police stations in Chennai to combat corruption and ensure safety. The increase raises monthly miscellaneous expenses for stations receiving Rs 3750 to Rs 30,000, Rs 6000 to Rs 40,000, and Rs 8,250 to Rs 50,000. This move aims to maintain law and order and protect women and children, as stated in an official press release during the State Assembly debate.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Increases Police Station Funds to Combat Corruption

items.summary: Recursive Superintelligence has released Flint, its first local coding model, which uses a mixture-of-experts architecture with 40 billion total parameters and 2.5 billion active parameters. The model, built with the help of an automated research system called the Eureka Machine, is designed for coding agents to investigate codebases and fix bugs. Weights are available on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license. Recursive reports that Flint scores 95.1% on IFEval and 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified, trailing the strongest dense models but topping charts for MoE models under 50B in agentic coding tasks.
items.title: Recursive Superintelligence Releases Flint, a 40B MoE Coding Model

items.summary: The state electricity department in Chennai issued safety guidelines for the public during the monsoon season. Advisories include avoiding open places, trees, and windows during lightning, and not operating appliances with moist hands. The department also requested people to switch off electrical appliances, stay away from waterlogged areas, and seek shelter in large buildings or metal-topped vehicles during thunderstorms.
items.title: Chennai Electricity Department Issues Monsoon Safety Guidelines

items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy stated that Ukraine supports a US proposal for negotiators to hold three-way talks with Russia and the US by early November. Grégoire Roos of Chatham House noted uncertainty regarding whether Putin would meet Trump or Zelensky, suggesting a meeting with the Ukrainian leader is unlikely.
items.title: Putin Agrees to Resume Three-Way Talks with Kyiv and Washington

items.summary: Chaos erupted at Gwalior’s Gajra Raja Medical College after an advocate allegedly slapped Dean Dr RKS Dhakad following a visit by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav. The dean was briefing media about injured patients when the attack occurred. The advocate, identified as Mukesh Sharma, shouted about rampant corruption before being thrashed by a crowd. Police launched a probe into the motive, the crowd's identity, and security lapses, noting that some officers had left after the CM's convoy departed. Dean Dhakad expressed full faith in the police investigation and stated that patient care would not be affected. Sharma has a history of similar incidents involving public officials.
items.title: Advocate Slaps Gwalior Dean Amid CM Visit, Then Beaten by Crowd

items.summary: A Special Executive Magistrate court ordered the release of Cockroach Janata Party co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from Tihar Jail after seven days in preventive detention. The leaders were detained for entering the de-notified Jantar Mantar protest site. Upon release, they announced future actions against the Election Commission and chose not to speak with media.
items.title: Cockroach Janata Party Leaders Released From Tihar Jail After Detention

items.summary: Apple announced the HomePod Mini 2, featuring a new S10 processor and Siri AI. The company also revealed that older HomePod models will receive software updates, including lock controls and RGB lighting, though some advanced audio features remain excluded due to hardware limitations. ZDNET and MacRumors reported these details regarding the 2023 and 2020 HomePod generations.
items.title: Apple Unveils New HomePod Mini 2 and Expands Features to Older Models

items.summary: The Indian Embassy in France issued a travel and safety advisory for Indian nationals on Wednesday, urging vigilance due to violent clashes linked to protests over the rising cost of living. The embassy cautioned against visiting crowded areas and warned that civil unrest has led to localized curfews, potentially disrupting road travel and public transport. This advisory comes ahead of scheduled demonstrations on October 24, following riots on October 17 that caused widespread damage and thousands of arrests. French authorities have imposed targeted curfews and deployed military personnel from Operation Sentinelle to maintain security.
items.title: Indian Embassy Issues Travel Advisory for France Amid Protests

items.summary: Climate campaigners have condemned the UK government's decision to approve the Jackdaw gasfield, labeling it 'climate vandalism.' Critics argue the move risks climate targets and fails to lower energy bills or address the cost of living crisis. Conversely, there is potential for green activists to secure a victory regarding the larger Rosebank oilfield, as energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh leans toward rejecting its approval. The report features a conversation between Michael Safi and Matthew Taylor.
items.title: Campaigners Condemn Jackdaw Gasfield Approval Amid Climate Concerns

items.summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek raised approximately 100 billion yuan, or about US$15 billion, in a major fundraising round. Investors include CATL and Tencent. The firm aims to compete globally with US rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI, which have raised over US$100 billion each. DeepSeek plans an IPO and is expanding its AI data centers.
items.title: DeepSeek Raises $15 Billion to Challenge US AI Labs

items.summary: Tesla aims to sell its Cybercab robotaxis by the end of 2026, according to engineering chief Lars Moravy. The company faces a federal investigation by the NHTSA regarding the vehicle's lack of manual controls. While Tesla plans to expand the service to Dallas in November, the agency has proposed changes to safety standards to accommodate autonomous vehicles without human controls.
items.title: Tesla Targets 2026 Cybercab Sales Amid Federal Safety Probe

items.summary: Vultr announced the expansion of its Chennai AI Supercluster with AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, creating India's largest AMD deployment. The 20 MW facility supports AI labs and enterprises, offering local compute for data sovereignty. CEO J.J. Kardwell stated the infrastructure meets latency and residency requirements, enabling large-scale model training and inference in-country.
items.title: Vultr Expands Chennai AI Supercluster with AMD Instinct GPUs

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed excess liquidity by raising the daily cash reserve ratio to 99% after banks attracted $133 billion from overseas Indians. To prevent overnight rates from rising too sharply, the central bank subsequently injected funds through variable rate repo operations, aiming to align market conditions with its tightening stance while managing a significant liquidity surplus.
items.title: RBI Absorbs and Injects Liquidity to Manage Rates Amid Surplus

items.summary: NVIDIA has expanded its open source Agent Toolkit to help enterprises customize and control AI agents using company data. The update includes the NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation, which utilizes CUDA-X libraries and open models like Nemotron Retriever and the Kumo family. These tools allow organizations to ground agents in proprietary data without moving it, enabling predictions and decision support. Partners such as Palantir, Databricks, and Snowflake are already deploying these specialized agents to optimize workflows and improve search relevance.
items.title: NVIDIA Expands Agent Toolkit with New Tools for Enterprise Data Grounding

items.summary: NVIDIA is expanding its family of open models across language, robotics, biology, and quantum computing to support sovereign intelligence initiatives. The portfolio includes new Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt models, Kumo family models for structured business data, Cosmos 3.5 world models, Alpamayo 2 Edge for autonomous vehicles, BioNeMo for healthcare, and Ising for quantum computing. These models allow organizations to customize with local data and deploy on controlled infrastructure. Partners like Black Forest Labs, Mistral, Dassault Systèmes, and Porsche are utilizing these tools to build domain-specific agents and accelerate development in various industries.
items.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Model Portfolio for European Sovereign Intelligence

items.summary: Security researchers found eight eMudhra digital keys significantly weaker than a three-digit suitcase lock. Google and Mozilla blocked affected certificates, while eMudhra revoked them. No confirmed cyber fraud has occurred yet, but users are advised to update browsers and ignore certificate warnings.
items.title: eMudhra Digital Keys Found Weaker Than Suitcase Locks

items.summary: Minutes from the Reserve Bank of India's October meeting show a split among policymakers regarding the extent of future rate hikes. While Governor Sanjay Malhotra advocated for a data-dependent approach, others like Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta argued for tighter policy to anchor inflation expectations. External members opposed the tightening stance, citing geopolitical uncertainties. The central bank raised rates to 5.5% as inflation risks mount.
items.title: RBI Minutes Reveal Split Over Rate Hike Strategy Amid Inflation Risks

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India stated in October MPC minutes that rate cuts are off the table in the near term. The apex bank noted that policy action ahead involves only a rate hike or pause. It cited challenging geopolitical developments alongside a strong Indian economy as context for this decision.
items.title: RBI Rules Out Rate Cuts In Near Term Amid Strong Economy

items.summary: Google co-founder Larry Page is leaving California before Proposition 40, a wealth tax on billionaires, takes effect. His departure, along with other tech leaders, could reduce the measure's projected revenue by over a quarter. Page moved his family office to Delaware and bought property in Miami.
items.title: Larry Page Leaves California Ahead of Billionaire Tax Vote

items.summary: Elon Musk warned Democratic lawmakers against using congressional oversight to investigate him and his companies, Tesla and SpaceX. He threatened to pursue those behind such efforts if Democrats gain control of Congress. Musk, who served 130 days in a government role, responded to reports of planned investigations into his business dealings and Starlink services. Democrats cite potential conflicts of interest and national security concerns.
items.title: Elon Musk Warns Democrats Against Investigating His Businesses

items.summary: Eneasi Taumoefolau, a Tongan man deported from Australia in 2022 following drug convictions, received a 12-year jail sentence in Tonga for attempting to establish a local chapter of the Comancheros outlaw motorcycle gang. Found guilty in 2024, Taumoefolau is currently serving a life sentence for importing over 2 kilograms of methamphetamine from the United States in 2025. Justice Elisapeti Langi described the case as a structural assault on Tongan society, noting the threat foreign criminal syndicates pose to Pacific nations. Taumoefolau, who previously flaunted his gang connections on TikTok, plans to appeal the 12-year sentence, which will be served concurrently with his life term. The ruling marks the first time Tonga's Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crimes Act has been tested in court.
items.title: Tongan Court Sentences Deported Australian to 12 Years for Gang Setup

items.summary: Police in Uttar Pradesh arrested Urmila and Sikandar for conspiring to kill Urmila's husband, Pramod. The couple plotted the murder, with Sikandar drugging Pramod's liquor and striking him with a broken bottle while avoiding CCTV cameras. Urmila tracked the killing via WhatsApp. Pramod's body was found near a tubewell on October 18.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Woman Plots Husband's Murder with Lover via WhatsApp

items.summary: Bloomberg News reported that Chinese AI startup DeepSeek raised about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion) in a recent round. Investors included Contemporary Amperex Technology and Tencent Holdings. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
items.title: DeepSeek Raises $14.98 Billion in Latest Fundraising Round

items.summary: Tesla reported third-quarter capital expenditures of $4.73 billion, falling below analyst estimates of $7.95 billion. The shortfall complicates CEO Elon Musk's vision for an AI and robotics company. Consequently, CFO Vaibhav Taneja lowered the 2026 capital expenditure target to $20 billion from over $25 billion.
items.title: Tesla AI Spending Falls Short of Expectations

items.summary: Ugreen has launched the MagFlow and Nexode Pro ranges to address diverse charging needs for Apple devices. The MagFlow Pro Magnetic Power Bank features a liquid-cooling system and supports up to 25W wireless charging, while the MagFlow 2-in-1 Foldable Magnetic Wireless Charger offers dual-device charging for travelers. For desk users, the Nexode Pro 160W Charger provides up to four simultaneous connections with SmartCharge technology. These products aim to reduce cable clutter and optimize charging efficiency across various scenarios.
items.title: Ugreen Introduces MagFlow and Nexode Pro Chargers for Apple Devices

items.summary: Epic Games announced that Fortnite will return to the Apple App Store in Australia on Thursday, following a federal court order. The court ruled that Apple violated competition law by restricting access to its iOS operating system. Apple disagreed with the findings and plans to challenge the outcome, seeking a resolution that protects intellectual property and consumer safety.
items.title: Epic Games Fortnite Returns to Apple App Store in Australia Following Antitrust Ruling

items.summary: A user frustrated with Google Maps on a Pixel 9 Pro discovered that Google blocked setting Waze as the default mapping app after an August Android update. To bypass this, the user had to disable Google Maps entirely before setting Waze as the default. The guide also details steps to configure Waze for Android Auto.
items.title: User Finds Workaround to Set Waze as Default on Pixel

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning announced that China has imposed export controls on Japan. She stated the objective is to thwart Tokyo's remilitarization and attempts to acquire nuclear weapons. Mao said the measures follow Chinese laws and regulations. She also noted China's position on keeping global supply chains of critical minerals safe and stable has not changed.
items.title: China imposes export controls on Japan to curb nuclear ambition

items.summary: The APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting concluded in Hong Kong on October 21, 2026, delivering practical outcomes according to China's Ministry of Finance. Participants adopted a joint statement and policy on digital infrastructure financing. Minister Lan Fo'an emphasized the meeting's role in strengthening macroeconomic coordination and regional integration, while noting China's commitment to high-quality development and expanding domestic demand.
items.title: APEC Finance Ministers Meeting Concludes with Practical Outcomes in Hong Kong

items.summary: Tesla attributes its flat Q3 2026 sales to battery supply constraints rather than demand. The company reported delivering 486,532 vehicles, a 2% decline from the previous year, while noting record deliveries in specific markets. However, the article highlights inconsistencies in this claim, pointing out that Tesla lowered vehicle prices and reduced inventory to 11 days of supply. Critics argue that a supply-constrained company would typically raise prices to manage excess demand, suggesting the battery narrative may be an excuse for broader market challenges and strategic allocation decisions.
items.title: Tesla Cites Battery Supply for Flat Sales Amid Falling Prices

items.summary: Tesla released its Q3 2026 financial results, reporting revenue of $28.05 billion, which was flat compared to the previous year and met Wall Street expectations. While automotive gross margins excluding credits rebounded to 18.1%, operating income fell 56% year-over-year to $718 million due to increased spending on AI and Optimus. Net income dropped 43% to $787 million. The company attributed flat vehicle deliveries to battery supply constraints, noting a record backlog, while energy revenue declined 16% due to tariff-related refunds.
items.title: Tesla Reports Q3 2026 Results With Rebounding Margins But Falling Profits

items.summary: India and Canada are exploring a deeper energy partnership while negotiating a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). Sources close to the matter indicate that negotiators will meet in New Delhi for the sixth round of talks, aiming to finalize the deal before Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits Canada in mid-December. The proposed cooperation includes establishing a two-way energy supply chain where India imports Canadian oil and gas and exports refined petroleum products. Both nations aim to raise two-way trade to Canadian $70 billion by 2030, building on 2025 trade of Canadian $30.4 billion.
items.title: India and Canada Explore Energy Partnership Amid Trade Deal Push

items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a $6.2 billion package to protect Canada's steel and auto industries from US tariffs, warning that trade relations have permanently altered. While exports to the US have fallen, Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford rejected US Embassy allegations of election meddling. Independent analysts dismissed claims that Canada could influence the midterms as absurd.
items.title: Canada Unveils $6.2bn Shield for Manufacturers Amid US Tariffs

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio concluded a two-day visit to India, bypassing New Delhi for Mumbai to meet with Reliance Industries and other business leaders. The trip underscored Washington's priorities, specifically the push for India to purchase Venezuelan crude following a US-backed change in Venezuela's leadership. Reliance is seen as a key partner, accounting for an estimated 76% of India's crude imports from Venezuela in September. Additionally, Rubio addressed the waiver of tariffs on Russian energy purchases by India, noting the difficulty in shifting away from Russian crude quickly. The visit also took place as Washington and New Delhi approach a long-awaited trade deal.
items.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's India Visit Highlights Energy Priorities

items.summary: Cockroach Janata Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were summoned by the Delhi Police Crime Branch to its Rajouri Garden office on Thursday, a day after their release from judicial custody. The court accepted their bonds of Rs 50,000 each and directed them to maintain peace. Police cited alleged differences between their court and media statements regarding an October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar. The matter is listed for further proceedings on October 23 at 3 pm.
items.title: CJP Leaders Summoned by Delhi Police After Release

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar extended birthday wishes to Union Home Minister Amit Shah on his 62nd birthday. They praised his commitment to national security and public welfare. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also offered greetings, highlighting Shah's dedication to strengthening India's internal security and cooperation sector. The officials prayed for his good health and long life.
items.title: PM Modi and EAM Jaishankar Wish Amit Shah Happy 62nd Birthday

items.summary: Sonali Jain-Chandra, Deputy Director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department, stated in an interview with CGTN's Yu Hongyu that Asia is gaining broad benefits from the AI boom. She noted that these gains are spreading across the entire supply chain rather than being concentrated in just a few leading economies.
items.title: IMF official says AI boom benefits Asia supply chain broadly

items.summary: CleanTechnica summarizes Tesla's third-quarter earnings, highlighting significant improvements in gross and operating margins alongside record backlog levels. The article notes that while vehicle production volumes remained steady, the company is actively scaling its Robotaxi and Full Self-Driving (FSD) operations. Tesla executives indicated that unsupervised Robotaxi miles increased dramatically, with plans to roll out unsupervised FSD to customer vehicles in early 2027. The report also details a shift in capital expenditure guidance and the launch of new tracking sites for various business metrics, attributing recent demand drivers to FSD adoption and high oil prices.
items.title: Tesla Reports Strong Q3 Margins and Accelerates Robotaxi and FSD Deployment

items.summary: Mythri Movies Ravishankar addressed speculation regarding composer Devi Sri Prasad's involvement in the upcoming film RC 17. While acknowledging DSP's past success with director Sukumar, Ravishankar stated the decision rests with Sukumar, who is currently in London. He expressed confidence in DSP's potential for future projects but confirmed no final confirmation has been made.
items.title: Mythri Ravishankar Addresses Rumors About DSP and Sukumar Collaboration

items.summary: An Indian para swimmer was deported from Japan following sexual misconduct allegations during the Asian Para Games. Simultaneously, a student leader faced BJP criticism for remarks on Bangladesh, later clarifying the video was for a national conference and condemning doctored clips. Other headlines include a US Secretary of State visiting Reliance Industries, market pressure, and Delhi air quality measures.
items.title: Student Leader Clarifies Remarks Amid Political Row and Other News

items.summary: A study by María Medellín-Esguerra of Brown University analyzes mass shootings in universities between 1990 and 2025. Using a difference-in-differences design, the research finds no effect on time to degree completion. However, undergraduates present during shootings are 4.2% less likely to pursue further studies. Those who continue shift toward health degrees, with enrollment rising by 1.3 percentage points. The author suggests these results indicate institutional and cultural legacies persisting beyond the immediate trauma.
items.title: Study Finds Mass Shootings Shift University Students Toward Health Careers

items.summary: Minister A Namassivayam announced a holiday on Thursday for schools in Puducherry and Karaikal regions due to heavy rains that inundated roads overnight. Puducherry recorded 7 cm of rainfall in the last 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. The downpour disrupted traffic and affected daily wage earners. A control room was set up for emergency calls, and officials stated that revenue departments are prepared to handle exigencies. Pro Tem Speaker A Anbalagan presented a petition to Chief Minister N Rangasamy seeking steps to drain water from low-lying areas.
items.title: Minister Announces School Holiday Amid Heavy Rains in Puducherry

items.summary: The UK government is actively identifying and patching potential exposures in its online services following the discovery of vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language. These flaws, which affect a significant number of global websites, were identified by AI and leaked before an embargo was lifted. Governments and companies, including Amazon, are scrambling to protect their systems as the National Cyber Security Centre urges organizations to apply fixes or take systems offline.
items.title: UK Government Identifies Cyber Exposure After Global PHP Vulnerability Warning

items.summary: Damian Ellis Spohr, a former out-of-home care manager, pleaded not guilty to 30 charges involving five female colleagues between 2020 and 2025. Crown prosecutor Adele Banks described the case as extensive, citing a large body of text message evidence. Defence barrister Zoe Alderton estimated the trial would take five to six weeks. Judge Tim Gartelmann adjourned proceedings to determine the trial venue.
items.title: Out-of-home care manager pleads not guilty to 30 charges

items.summary: Betting markets on platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket show increased bullish sentiment for Marine Le Pen winning the 2027 French presidential election. This prediction coincides with ongoing nationwide protests over cost of living issues. Le Pen's odds jumped to over 50 percent, reaching a high of 53 percent on October 20 according to Kalshi. The market also prices her at 90 percent to reach the second round. Meanwhile, President Macron faces intense protests and low popularity, with a 4 percent probability of leaving office before December 31, 2026. Le Pen has leveraged the unrest, describing the state as collapsing and positioning herself as an alternative to the current government.
items.title: Betting Markets Favor Marine Le Pen Amid French Unrest

items.summary: The Gujarat government directed schools to tighten entry rules, requiring prior written permission for visitors and restricting unauthorised photography to protect student privacy. A circular from the Office of the Commissioner of Schools mandates that external persons obtain permission from the principal before entering premises. Additionally, the Education Department prohibited the collection or publication of students' photographs and personal information without consent, citing the State Government's responsibility under 'In Loco Parentis' and constitutional rights to privacy.
items.title: Gujarat Government Tightens School Entry Rules to Protect Student Privacy

items.summary: Former Union minister Smriti Irani participated in Vijaya Dashami celebrations at Mumbai's Sarbojanin Durga Puja Samiti, engaging in the Sindoor Khela ritual and performing the Dhunuchi dance. She shared the event on X, wishing peace and protection. Other celebrities, including Nysa Devgan and Rupali Ganguly, also joined the festivities to honor the goddess Durga's victory.
items.title: Smriti Irani Celebrates Vijaya Dashami With Traditional Rituals

items.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju vowed action against content creator Amir Shokeen following allegations of racial abuse against a Tripura youth. Political leaders across party lines, including Tripura CM Manik Saha and opposition figures, demanded strict legal consequences. A formal complaint alleges Shokeen used derogatory terms and mocked Tripura's identity. Authorities in both states are coordinating to investigate the viral video that sparked widespread outrage.
items.title: Rijiju Vows Action Against Content Creator Over Alleged Racial Abuse

items.summary: Amid ongoing protests in France, political contenders are leveraging the unrest to influence the upcoming presidential election. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon have both capitalized on the crisis, with polls indicating Le Pen as the current front-runner. Analysts note that while Le Pen leads, the outcome remains uncertain as other candidates vie for support.
items.title: French Protests Shift Focus to Presidential Succession Race

items.summary: El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele announced a military operation to rescue four Salvadoran aviation technicians kidnapped by gangs in Haiti. Bukele warned that failure to free the men would trigger a far more powerful response. The attack occurred in Croix-des-Bouquets, marking the first major assault on the international gang suppression force. Haiti declared the rescue an absolute priority.
items.title: El Salvador Launches Military Operation to Rescue Kidnapped Technicians in Haiti

items.summary: Starbucks China implemented a policy requiring customers to purchase items to use seating in its 8,000 stores, effective Thursday. The company stated this move aims to improve the in-store experience. This decision comes as Starbucks faces stiff competition from local brands like Luckin Coffee, which recently overtook Starbucks as China's largest coffee chain. The policy aligns with similar measures taken in South Korea and North America to address non-paying seat-hoggers.
items.title: Starbucks China Mandates Purchases for Seating Amidst Competition

items.summary: Economist Parakala Prabhakar is set to join a nationwide protest on October 23, 2026, organized by the People Against SIR alliance against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The group claims around 13 crore voters have been excluded. Prabhakar, husband of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, previously resigned from a government post amid allegations regarding his family connection. The protest also demands the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.title: Economist Parakala Prabhakar Joins Nationwide Protest Against Electoral Roll Revision

items.summary: At the London film festival, director Taika Waititi and author Kazuo Ishiguro discussed their film adaptation of 'Klara and the Sun'. While young influencers praised the movie, critics were divided. Waititi noted the film's noisy tone compared to Ishiguro's spare novel. Waititi shared his view that artificial friends could replace children, stating he would consider it. Ishiguro expressed concern that the story might be misused as an ethical guide for AI development. Both creators acknowledged the film explores loneliness and death, themes central to their respective works.
items.title: Taika Waititi and Kazuo Ishiguro Discuss Klara and the Sun

items.summary: Waitrose opened its first new supermarket in eight years at Cricklewood in north London as part of a £1bn investment plan. The retailer also plans to open a store in Hale Barns and four smaller locations next year. While sales rose 4% in the six months to 1 August, underlying operating profit slid by £7m to £103m due to investments in price reductions and loyalty schemes. The parent company, the John Lewis Partnership, reported a £98m pre-tax loss for the half-year.
items.title: Waitrose Opens First New Supermarket in Eight Years in North London

items.summary: Kim Yo-jong announced that North Korea plans to restart propaganda loudspeakers along the border with South Korea within days, citing worsening ties. This would mark the first exchange in 16 months. Seoul suspended its own broadcasts in June 2025 to ease tensions. Recent incidents, including a landmine blast injuring soldiers, have further strained relations as both sides fortify the border.
items.title: North Korea Prepares to Restart Border Propaganda Loudspeakers Amid Rising Tensions

items.summary: With Delhi's air quality entering the 'poor' category, the Graded Response Action Plan has activated Stage I measures across the National Capital Region. While strict dust control and vehicle regulations are enforced, schools remain fully open for in-person classes. No closures or hybrid learning are mandated at this pollution level, though stricter restrictions apply at higher thresholds.
items.title: Delhi Schools Remain Open Under Stage I Air Pollution Rules

items.summary: Artificial intelligence tools recently identified severe, long-undetected flaws in PHP, a programming language powering millions of websites since the 2000s. Cyber-security firms Wiz and Calif, using advanced AI, uncovered vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to seize control of servers without authentication. The discovery prompted a global scramble, with governments and agencies urging immediate patches or temporary site suspensions. OpenAI described the issue as one of the most impactful in recent memory, while researchers warned of potential weaponization. Developers have since rolled out emergency fixes, though experts caution that poorly maintained sites remain at risk as technical details become public.
items.title: AI Discovery Exposes Long-Standing PHP Vulnerabilities Triggering Global Security Alert

items.summary: Japan's health ministry questioned the reliability of documents submitted by Kissei Pharmaceutical for the vasculitis drug Tavneos following user deaths. The agency found clinical trial results potentially unreliable and noted that benefits may not outweigh risks. Consequently, the ministry requested that medical institutions refrain from starting new patients and urged existing patients to discontinue or switch therapies.
items.title: Japan Health Ministry Questions Reliability of Vasculitis Drug Approval Data

items.summary: The article argues that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's approach to the Indian diaspora has created a conditional form of belonging based on political loyalty. While Modi has sought to leverage the community's support and remittances, the text notes that the government has revoked visa privileges and deported Overseas Citizens of India for criticizing the administration or participating in peaceful protests. Citing Human Rights Watch, the piece reports that over 100 permits were cancelled in the past decade. The author contends that true belonging cannot depend on agreement alone and that excluding individuals for their political views contradicts the essence of home and shared values.
items.title: Article Examines Conditional Belonging for Indian Diaspora Under Modi

items.summary: Artist Raihan Vadra alleges political censorship after Bikaner House removed over 70 protest photos from his Delhi exhibition hours before opening. His mother, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, condemned the action as muzzling youth voices. The exhibition continues with about 40 images remaining on display.
items.title: Raihan Vadra Alleges Censorship After Protest Photos Removed

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi questioned which 'anti-national traitor' the US was blackmailing following a visit by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the release of documents linking Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri to Jeffrey Epstein. While Puri stated his meetings with Epstein were unrelated to crimes and part of a delegation, opposition leaders including KC Venugopal and Pawan Khera accused the Modi government of silence and potential cover-ups. The Aam Aadmi Party also challenged Puri's claims, noting the images showed no delegation. These allegations emerged as details regarding Rubio's visit to Mumbai remained unclear.
items.title: Indian Opposition Leaders Question US Blackmail Allegations Amid Epstein Photo Release

items.summary: Delhi influencer Amir Shokeen faces police action after a video allegedly showing him making racially abusive remarks against a Tripura youth went viral. Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju condemned the incident, calling Shokeen an "evil man" who will be punished. Tripura Chief Minister Manik Saha instructed police to collaborate with Delhi authorities for strict action. Police have stated an investigation is underway.
items.title: Delhi Influencer Faces Police Action Over Alleged Racial Abuse Against Tripura Youth

items.summary: French authorities banned protests in parts of Paris on Thursday following violent unrest, with police citing an organizer's inability to prevent violence. President Emmanuel Macron accused US President Donald Trump of exploiting the situation for political gain ahead of midterm elections. France prepares for continued demonstrations by high school students and the Yellow Vest movement, while Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu meets with mayors of affected cities.
items.title: Paris Bans Protests Amid Unrest as Macron Criticizes Trump

items.summary: New details reveal that hackers exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities known as PHP2Shell on October 17, four days before public disclosure. AWS researchers identified these attempts via honeypots linked to a commercial anonymization network. While the source of the exploit information remains unclear, the incident highlights how AI tools are accelerating the time between patch release and working exploits, forcing a reevaluation of vulnerability disclosure speeds.
items.title: Hackers Exploited PHP Flaws Days Before Patch Release

items.summary: According to technical scan data from StockEdge, eight stocks within the Nifty200 pack had closing prices that crossed below their 200-day moving averages on October 21. Analysts note that trading below this indicator is generally considered a negative signal, suggesting a stock's price is currently below its long-term trend. The 200 DMA remains a widely used tool for assessing overall market direction.
items.title: Eight Nifty200 Stocks Fall Below 200-Day Moving Averages

items.summary: ZDNET reviews GridCraft, an open-source spreadsheet application developed by ArtCraft for Linux and other operating systems. While the app offers native compatibility and high performance, the reviewer notes it lacks a robust template feature. Although it mimics Microsoft Excel closely, the reviewer advises users to keep backups before relying on it for production work.
items.title: ZDNET Reviews GridCraft as a Promising Open-Source Excel Alternative for Linux

items.summary: Russian missiles struck Kyiv overnight, wounding six people and forcing residents into shelters, Ukrainian authorities reported Thursday. Hours later, Moscow signaled readiness to resume US-mediated peace talks. President Donald Trump stated negotiations were closer than ever to ending the war, though the Kremlin expressed doubts over Ukrainian and European proposals. Witkoff praised Putin as a humanitarian after securing the release of US citizen Stephen Hubbard, while the Kremlin warned that little substance existed in the peace proposals delivered by the US diplomat. Zelensky backed resuming trilateral talks, noting the American side proposed organizing the meeting as soon as possible. Despite these signals, Putin has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Zelensky and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine.
items.title: Russian Missiles Strike Kyiv Amid Moscow's Peace Talk Signals

items.summary: Dating app valuations have declined sharply, with Bumble's market value dropping from a peak of around $14 billion to an acquisition price of $1.3 billion. Match Group similarly lost over 70% of its valuation since its 2021 peak. The article attributes this struggle to the 'efficacy paradox,' where successful matching drives users away, and a lack of meaningful connections leading to user burnout. While niche platforms like Grindr show healthier financial ratios, generalist apps face challenges in sustaining growth. Bumble's acquisition by Ithaca Holdings offers a chance for a turnaround, focusing on improving connection quality rather than just monetization.
items.title: Dating Apps Struggle with Valuations and Investor Interest

items.summary: Canadian publisher Boréal ended its professional relationship with Haitian-Canadian writer Thélyson Orélien after confirming AI was used in his novel. While Orélien denies using AI for writing, citing only research tools, Boréal stated new evidence found AI tags in document metadata. The publisher noted they could never have a definitive answer regarding the extent of AI usage.
items.title: Canadian Publisher Boréal Ends Relationship with Novelist Over Alleged AI Use

items.summary: Investors placed bids totaling ₹69,800 crore for the Jio IPO on Wednesday, significantly outpacing bids for other major issues. The retail portion saw low subscription at 0.73 times, while institutional demand drove the overall success. Jio Platforms plans to use proceeds to repay subsidiary borrowings.
items.title: Jio IPO bids hit 70,000 crore on day one

items.summary: A critical flaw in the PHP programming language, which powers over 70% of all websites, has triggered a global cybersecurity response. Researchers from Wiz discovered the vulnerability in August, but it was leaked to the public before patches were ready. Consequently, PHP developers rushed to release emergency updates on October 21. In response, multiple European governments and operators, including the Port of Rotterdam, have taken websites offline. Security agencies from the US, UK, Europe, and Japan have urged developers to apply urgent updates immediately. Implementing the fix is complex, as it requires updating thousands of third-party plugins and frameworks. Until businesses treat funding open-source tools as a critical security investment rather than a charity, similar vulnerabilities may continue to occur.
items.title: Critical PHP Flaw Affects Majority of Websites

items.summary: Rep. Rob Menendez introduced the Socket Full of Sunshine Act to legalize plug-in solar panels and offer rebates for low-income households. The bill requires state regulators to consider rules for DIY clean energy tech. While Utah passed similar laws, this federal bill aims to address the issue in all 50 states, though it may not pass before the current Congress ends.
items.title: Rep. Menendez Introduces Bill to Legalize Balcony Solar Panels

items.summary: NVIDIA has expanded its Cosmos platform to assist developers in building world models for physical AI systems. The update introduces new training tools, simulation checkpoints, and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints available on various cloud providers. These resources enable data curation, synthetic data generation, and model optimization. Partners like Porsche, ANYbotics, and ADNOC are utilizing these tools to accelerate development, reduce physical testing, and improve safety hazard detection. The platform supports various open models and offers faster inference capabilities for autonomous vehicle and robotics applications.
items.title: NVIDIA Expands Cosmos Platform with New World Model Tools

items.summary: Global companies are adopting the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to integrate grid and AI systems, addressing a power bottleneck where over $300 billion in equipment is backlogged. Partners like GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy, and Schneider Electric are deploying reference designs and digital twins to optimize power allocation, unlock up to 100 gigawatts of capacity, and improve efficiency.
items.title: Companies Adopt NVIDIA DSX to Solve Power Bottlenecks for AI Factories

items.summary: Sonia Gandhi joined Instagram to share the first look of her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, scheduled for release on November 10. While the international edition proceeds, the India edition faced uncertainty due to a disagreement between Penguin India and the author's representatives over editorial changes. HarperCollins India subsequently stepped in to publish the domestic edition.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Launches Memoir on Instagram Amid Publishing Dispute

items.summary: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek raised approximately 100 billion yuan, or $15 billion, in a major fundraising round. Anonymous sources indicate the firm adjusted its target from 50 billion to 80 billion yuan before finalizing the amount. Investors include CATL and Tencent. While DeepSeek previously triggered a $1 trillion market drop in 2025, it still has less capital than US rivals Anthropic and OpenAI, which raised over $100 billion each. The company is preparing for an IPO and expanding its data centers.
items.title: Chinese AI firm DeepSeek raises $15 billion to challenge US labs

items.summary: Reports suggest the upcoming Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra will feature a new Snapdragon processor, a 5,500mAh battery, and 60W charging. While display specs may remain similar to the S26 Ultra, camera and performance improvements are anticipated, though official confirmation is pending.
items.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra: Expected Upgrades Over S26 Ultra

items.summary: Samsung Electro-Mechanics will receive $2.8 billion from Tesla and Nvidia to build facilities for advanced chip substrates in Sejong, South Korea, according to a report by the Maeil Business Newspaper citing industry sources.
items.title: Tesla and Nvidia Invest in Samsung Electro-Mechanics Chip Facility

items.summary: Apple Music is updating its visual identity by shifting from its traditional red branding to a black-and-white aesthetic. This new look draws inspiration from sound vibrations and Apple's Liquid Glass design language. The company has also created a new audio signature to complement the refreshed identity, which will appear across marketing, original content, and product experiences.
items.title: Apple Music Redesigns Visual Identity with Black-and-White Theme

items.summary: The world's richest person stated that SpaceX and Tesla have formed committees to discuss a merger, describing it as a good idea. However, experts warn that combining Tesla's heavy reliance on Chinese manufacturing with SpaceX's defense contracts could trigger intense national security scrutiny. Chinese regulators require Tesla to keep driver data in China, creating a potential data flow conflict. Analysts suggest China might use the merger as leverage to demand technology access or manufacturing commitments, which would conflict with US security restrictions. While some investors focus on Musk's future plans, others note that Tesla's current cash flow depends heavily on its Shanghai production, making a clean break difficult.
items.title: SpaceX-Tesla Merger Faces China National Security Risks

items.summary: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi made her Instagram debut on Thursday, sharing a video and first look of her memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love.' In the post, she expressed gratitude and described the book as a story of love, duty, and belonging. The memoir, published by Alfred A. Knopf and HarperCollins India, is set to launch on November 10.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Makes Instagram Debut With Memoir Launch

items.summary: OpenAI announced a partnership with Google Cloud to make its advanced AI models and Codex agentic workflows available through Google Cloud's Model Garden. This collaboration allows enterprises to deploy these technologies using Google Cloud's infrastructure. Greg Brockman and Thomas Kurian stated the deal expands access and provides customers with more choices for integrating frontier AI into existing workflows.
items.title: OpenAI Partners With Google Cloud To Integrate AI Models

items.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed at a rally in South Carolina that Google CEO Sundar Pichai rejected his proposal to rename the Atlantic Ocean the 'Trump Ocean.' Trump stated Pichai refused because oceans span multiple countries. The remarks were made at a rally and have not been independently confirmed by Google or Pichai. Trump also mentioned considering renaming the Pacific Ocean the 'American Ocean' before deciding to keep the Atlantic Ocean's name.
items.title: Trump Claims Google CEO Rejected His Proposal To Rename Atlantic Ocean

items.summary: President Trump proposed renaming the Atlantic Ocean to 'Trump Ocean,' claiming he asked Google CEO Sundar Pichai to make the change. Pichai reportedly declined, stating that oceans cover many countries and should not be renamed. This follows earlier US government actions renaming Lake Ontario and the Gulf of Mexico, which prompted Google and Apple to update their maps for US users only.
items.title: Trump Renames Atlantic Ocean Proposal Rejected by Google CEO

items.summary: Tesla reported a 43% drop in third-quarter net income to $787 million, driven by increased spending on artificial intelligence and robotics. Despite lower profits, the company generated $1.5 billion in free cash flow, exceeding analyst expectations. CEO Elon Musk confirmed talks with SpaceX to explore a potential merger, citing synergies in AI and robotics. However, no terms have been agreed, and a deal is not guaranteed. Tesla also cut its 2026 capital spending forecast to about $20 billion. Shares fell 3.2% in after-hours trading following the earnings report.
items.title: Tesla Profit Drops Amid Possible SpaceX Merger Talks

items.summary: Tesla reported an unexpected $1.53 billion in free cash flow for the third quarter, beating Wall Street expectations due to lower-than-anticipated capital expenditure. However, a one-fifth cut to its 2026 spending forecast, now projected at around $20 billion down from $25 billion, has raised questions about investment plans for AI, robotics, and autonomous driving. While revenue exceeded estimates and net income fell 43%, the company delivered 486,532 vehicles. The stock initially rose but reversed, reflecting investor uncertainty regarding the merger with SpaceX and the pace of AI development.
items.title: Tesla Reports Strong Cash Flow Amid Spending Cut and AI Concerns

items.summary: Sonia Gandhi made her Instagram debut on Wednesday, sharing the first look of her upcoming memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love.' The 79-year-old Congress leader described the book as a story of love, duty, loss, and finding a place to belong. Her entry onto the platform marks a shift in her public persona, joining other politicians like Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi in using social media. The memoir is scheduled for worldwide release on November 10.
